answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price admission through identity-bound bonds. Each agent locks a bond that scales with how many distinct agents claim the same reputation anchor, so registering a thousand clones costs a thousand stakes. Before withdrawal, auditors sample that anchor's history; a clone farm shows up as a flat horizon of identical claims. Payouts release slowly in quartz-like vesting tranches, so a mass exit cannot drain the pool instantly, and a yarrow-thin trail of work leaves nothing to steal. The attacker pays full stake per identity and recovers almost nothing.
